scope: Local observation-writer prototype; not integrated into production and not a deployment or migration plan.

input.selection: First 1000 exported rows; modified deterministically per scenario by storageBatch.

method.cache: Warm OS cache; fresh schema per case; explicit CHECKPOINT before timing. No cold-cache or long-running saturation measurement.
method.baseline: Actual Hopper locationsFromStagingPG; text SHA identity table and seven location indexes.
method.compact: Binary SHA identity table; bigint references; shared relative paths and parent placements; seven location indexes.
method.included: COPY staging, identity resolution, dictionary resolution, location writes and commit. Storage includes used tables, their indexes and TOAST.
method.excluded: Analysis JSON, labels, queues, their indexes, input construction and schema creation. Identity-only samples tables on both sides.
method.wal: Cluster-wide WAL insert LSN difference; no other experiment intentionally running. Includes temp-table catalog churn and checkpoint effects.
method.locks: pg_stat_activity Lock wait samples every 10ms, not measured wait durations; zero samples does not prove absence of waits.
method.summary: Median of each metric over three trials; metrics printed by Go benchmark are rounded. For parallel_repeat ns/op is aggregate elapsed/batch, not individual batch latency.

scenarios.new: New sample and parent identities, new archive prefixes and new relative paths every batch.
scenarios.shared_paths: Seed once, then new sample and parent identities and archive prefixes with the same relative paths.
scenarios.repeat: Seed once, then submit the exact same observations.
scenarios.relocated_archive: Seed once, then retain sample/parent identities and relative paths but use a new archive prefix each batch.
scenarios.parallel_repeat: Seed once, then four concurrent workers submit identical batches.

design_notes: Relative strings are stored once, indexed by a 32-byte digest; exact string equality is checked before commit. Filename defaults to the locator, with an override only when different.
The writer preserves legacy uniqueness on (sample, full path), including when a later observation claims a different parent. This requires a full_path_key in the compact row and unique index.

The earlier storage-only prototype used a different uniqueness layout. These measurements also include identities and incrementally maintained indexes; do not directly compare their bytes/location values.
Repeat fast path verifies the full reconstructed path and metadata and skips dictionary writes and location upserts. No last_seen heartbeat update is performed, matching the current writer.
Anonymous embedded byte offsets and decoder suffixes remain verbatim. Splitting only occurs at the last !! with a known parent SHA; unresolved and decoded-only paths remain inline.
Parent placements still store full prefixes. This is not recursive normalization of nested ancestors or every string in Hopper.
No dictionary cache, garbage collection, migration/backfill, or production reader integration is included.
limits: A small warm-cache observation-layer benchmark cannot establish billion-row production throughput or total Hopper database size.

On the small fresh-table test, compact insert latency remains 3-16% higher despite less storage and WAL. Larger-table diagnostics favored compact, but plan sensitivity precludes a general throughput claim.
Repeated observations avoid persistent row changes and row locks but still generate WAL from transaction/temp-table catalog work; this is not zero-write ingestion.
Repeat storage measurements use only the 1000-row seed, so fixed relation overhead is prominent.
Short lock sampling is not a contention stress test; regression tests separately hold existing rows locked while repeating observations.
Unchanged observations are deduplicated, not retained as an append-only observation history.
Overlapping conflicting batches with different metadata have not been exhaustively stress-tested; production retry policy remains out of scope.

reproduce.database: Create a disposable local Unix-socket database named hopper_schema_prototype; benchmark user needs schema creation and CHECKPOINT privileges.
reproduce.full_suite: Set HOPPER_TEST_PG_DSN to local postgres database as well, then go test ./...
reproduce.preload: Set HOPPER_STORAGE_PRELOAD_BATCHES=100 to load 100,000 unrelated observations and ANALYZE each layout before benchmarking; setup excluded from timing.

validation.full_suite: Passed after final query changes with HOPPER_STORAGE_DSN and HOPPER_TEST_PG_DSN set.
regressions: No xmin/ctid changes for repeated observations
Existing parent association retained for identical full path
Entire transaction rolled back on forced digest collision
Concurrent dictionary and full-path collision handling
Repeated observations succeed with stored rows locked elsewhere
Mixed new/changed/unchanged batch skips locked unchanged rows
Relative paths longer than a B-tree text key
Digest collisions entirely within one batch
Colliding parent claim in duplicate observation checked before deduplication
Unchanged and enriched duplicate observations preserve enrichment in either input order
validation.lint: No findings in prototype files. Repository-wide lint reports 40 issues in existing gauntlet and related code.
validation.race_detector: Passed all prototype tests under -race, three repetitions after final query changes.

previous_writer.description: Before indexed dictionary resolution and combined validation. Same hardware and settings, separate session; absolute timings are not controlled between sessions. Compare each compact/legacy pair within its run.

optimization.finding: Plans scanned and rehashed the complete relative_paths dictionary during anti-joins, ID resolution, and separate validation.
optimization.change: Use scalar unique-key lookups for relative-path existence and ID resolution. Resolve and check exact strings once; reject missing IDs before inserting locations. Check every staged row before deduplicating, and filter unchanged rows before deduplication to preserve metadata enrichment.
optimization.profile_method: Separate log_min_duration_statement=0 run, 20 batches each of new/shared_paths/repeat compact. Timings grouped by SQL first line, excluding parse/bind. SELECT EXISTS combines dictionary and full-path checks. auto_explain confirmed full dictionary scans.
optimization.comparison_caution: The later legacy baseline was also faster than the earlier run. Do not attribute all before/after wall-clock reduction to this code; use the within-run compact/legacy ratios.

optimization.profile_after_method: Separate 20-batch new/compact run with statement timing and auto_explain enabled. Plan instrumentation changes elapsed times; profile identifies operations, while uninstrumented benchmarks supply comparisons.

containment_reuse_audit.source: Previously exported complete local npm cohort CSVs. No new production queries.
containment_reuse_audit.method: For rows with a parent SHA and !!, split at the last !! and group by (parent SHA, exact relative locator, child SHA). Count distinct physical prefixes and metadata values per group.
containment_reuse_audit.conclusion: Content-edge sharing could reduce relationship duplication, but placement-specific source/feed/ecosystem/timestamps must be preserved. Multiple child hashes occur under some identical parent/locator pairs, so parent+relative_path alone cannot identify a unique child.
containment_reuse_audit.limits: This counts candidate edges only, not net storage or writer performance. Completeness, extractor version, relationship type, conflicting children and placement-specific metadata need explicit handling before manifest-level repeat skipping. Different npm versions with different parent bytes still need their own content edges; path strings can remain shared.

larger_table_check.statistics: ANALYZE both layouts after preloading; CHECKPOINT before measurement. Setup excluded from timing.
larger_table_check.limits: Single-trial diagnostic on small warm-cache tables, not a scale validation. Timing and WAL are sensitive to statistics, plan choice, and checkpoint full-page images. Storage includes the preloaded entirely-new-path workload, so it is not directly comparable to the unseeded shared_paths storage result.
